<details><summary>Reading this synopsis</summary><ul>
<li>Reference periods are retained with each fact in the evidence file. Regional amounts and temperature departures are area-weighted grid summaries; station values describe individual locations.</li>
<li>Station peak rankings compare complete windows of the same length ending on the same calendar date in earlier years, with the current period included once in the rank count. They are not rankings of all calendar days or all weeks. At least 25 earlier complete windows are required; gaps and ties are retained. Peak anomalies compare matching window extrema with at least 15 complete 1991–2020 windows.</li>
<li>Precipitation includes rain and the liquid equivalent of snow. A freeze night has a daily minimum at or below 32°F. Dry-spell lengths use precipitation below 0.04 inch and are limited to their stated window; they are not necessarily ongoing spells. Supporting products may use a newer observation date than this synopsis cutoff.</li>
<li>Editorial focus follows supported rainfall, heat/cold and longer-term signals; no flood, damage or other impact is inferred from observations alone.</li>
<li>Regional snow interpretation is pending mountain/reference-area metrics; verified files alone do not establish a regional snow anomaly.</li>
<li>No compatible prior successful publication is available for comparison; no change since the previous publication is claimed.</li>
<li>PRISM, station and snow products have different reporting-time conventions. A shared cutoff date does not make their daily observation intervals identical.</li>
<li>Station network fractions use eligible fixed stations in AZ/NM, with complete current observations, publication screening and supported historical percentiles. ThreadEx series and ambiguous duplicate records are excluded. Comparison records differ among stations; these fractions are not land-area coverage. Day-to-day network-count changes are not interpreted without a matched station set.</li>
<li>Warm-day/cold-night counts use daily percentile thresholds; the frequency count itself is not historically ranked. A 14-day change in a rolling 30-day precipitation rank is not a precipitation amount or a change since yesterday.</li>
</ul></details>
</section>
